title: Check inherited contribution policy before research intake
applies_when: Adding a repository to a contribution scout: rules may live outside CONTRIBUTING, AI/human-review rules depend on contributor status, or a technically valid fix may not be publishable.
lesson: Check eligibility before expensive discovery and publication. GitHub can inherit the owner's .github rules, absent from the target clone: resolve the public html_url, pin and read them and linked guides/README rules. Pyee requires bot-emoji commit/changelog prefixes and reviewer disclosure, not a ban. Pallets' observed guide rejects AI-generated PRs/issues regardless of quality, including cleaning up or reusing them; do not assume an older trusted-contributor exception. Separate correctness, eligibility and interaction permission. Metadata exposes archived/disabled state and PR creation policy: has_pull_requests=true does not override collaborators_only. Public forks are not upstream PRs; interaction limits and per-user quotas also apply. Community profiles miss workflow-based guards: review observed workflow paths and their pinned actions, without executing them. A guard may use cross-repository activity or agent-prefixed branches; check exemptions and maintainer intent, never disguise provenance to evade it. Preserve private evidence, respect existing authors and redirect effort rather than bypass restrictions.
avoid_when: Missing documents/settings or failed reads are not permission. A minimal reproduction may not satisfy a demand for actual affected production code; never manufacture that witness. Standalone exploratory packets do not automatically inherit the repository question: retain it alongside the specific task, but do not retrofit frozen experiment arms. Timestamped settings and a permissive all value do not establish eligibility, available quota or written-policy compliance. A previous denial warrants investigation, not a permanent universal ban. Policies/limits change; do not transfer organization rules elsewhere, classify eligibility from keywords, or equate disclosure/human-review requirements with research bans. Internal tests and generic publish approval do not provide genuine human authorship. PR restrictions and bug-report eligibility are separate; inspect the actual issue policy. This lesson establishes no PR-yield or cost improvement.

evidence.note: Delegates contribution rules to Dask's linked development document; this two-line local guide is incomplete.

Observed 2026-10-18: AI assistance is allowed, but community speech and final PR prose require human-authored wording and personal review. An agent may open only a clearly labelled unsupervised Draft; generic publish approval is not that authorship. This is not a blanket research ban. Good-first-issue work is separately reserved for human learners. Recheck live rules before external action.

The pinned project guide requires bot-emoji prefixes and AI disclosure. Community-profile documents alone are not a complete guide index; explicit selection still needs review, not automatic permission.

The effective organization guide permits AI-assisted code but requires actual human review and forbids LLM-authored community speech, explicitly including PR descriptions and changelogs except translation/grammar. A passing privately tested repair still needs genuine human review and wording; a generic publish approval is not authorship. This guide is inherited even when the target clone has no CONTRIBUTING file.

This pinned template requires an open issue for nontrivial PRs and tox validation; a raw unittest run is not the requested complete contribution check. Read the actual test recipe before preparing a publication-ready change.

This agent guide carries useful contribution/test rules but also stale implementation claims: it says Python>=3.10 and deprecated cache=None/classmethod paths, while the same revision's pyproject requires >=3.11 and docs describe their removal. Separate workflow requirements from factual architecture summaries; verify the latter against current source and configuration.

This revision puts contribution rules in the README: generally open an issue before a PR, and assistant-found bug reports must show actual affected production code; sanitized examples are permitted but contrived ones are not. This is not a blanket AI ban or evidence that a synthetic reproduction is false.
GitHub documents default community files in the owner's .github repository, their location precedence and why inherited files are not present in individual clones.

Observed 2026-10-18 at Werkzeug intake: inherited rules reject AI-generated PRs/issues regardless of quality, including reopening, cleanup or reuse. Supersedes the earlier trusted-contributor interpretation. Intake stopped before model/setup/tests. Recheck current linked rules; no cross-organization or measured cost-saving claim.
GitHub documents temporary interaction restrictions, including collaborator-only participation that can prevent creating PRs independently of a project's written contribution guide.
GitHub separately supports disabling PRs and restricting their creation to collaborators; enabled features and written contribution guides are not a complete access decision.
Observed 2026-10-19: an opened-PR and scheduled workflow invokes a pinned unattended-pr guard with trusted-user/organization exemptions. Community-profile documents alone miss this rule.

The configured action documents cross-repository activity, comment style and agent-prefixed branches as closure signals, plus exemptions and maintainer overrides. Delivery risk is not code quality or a universal ban; no account verdict, accuracy or cost benefit is established. Do not rename or conceal AI provenance to evade the rule.

This revision requires a maintainer's /approve on a linked bug issue before an external fix PR and declines external feature PRs. It permits discussing reports first. Passing native tests, a personal fork or open PR creation settings are not that approval; choose the issue channel before preparing a publication-ready patch. Recheck the live rule before transfer.
